declarations.description: Idiomatic Lit `<rozie-sortable-list>` — a cross-framework drag-and-drop list compiled from one Rozie source via SortableJS. Two-way `items` (with an `items-change` event), keyboard reordering, cross-list drag, and a 4-verb handle.
declarations.name: SortableList

members.name: items
members.description: The bound items array. The sole `model: true` prop — two-way bind it (`r-model:items` / `v-model:items` / `bind:items` / `[(items)]`) and SortableList writes the re-ordered array back whenever a drag, cross-list move, or keyboard reorder commits, with no manual `onChange → setState` wiring.

members.name: itemKey
members.description: The per-row key the framework reconciler tracks each item by across a reorder — either a property name (e.g. `itemKey="id"` reads `item.id`) or an `(item, index) => key` function. With neither, id-less object items get a stable synthetic key via an internal `WeakMap` (survives reorder by object identity); primitive items fall back to index — pass a function for reorderable duplicate primitives.

members.name: handle
members.description: CSS selector identifying the per-row drag handle, so a drag starts only from that element rather than anywhere in the row. Authored class names render literally on every target (React included), so a plain `.grip` works; `$classSelector('grip')` is an optional, typo-checked way to author it.

members.name: group
members.description: SortableJS group name enabling cross-list drag — two lists sharing a `group` accept items between each other (the source fires `remove`, the destination fires `add`). Set `cloneable: true` to flip a string group into clone-mode. Lists that share a `group` also exchange rows by keyboard: Shift+arrow while a row is lifted hops it to the previous or next list of the same group (in source order), subject to the same pull/put rules as a mouse drag. `options.group` takes precedence over this prop, for keyboard hops as for drags. Function-valued `pull`/`put` cannot be evaluated without a drag, so those lists are unreachable by keyboard. Set `itemKey` on grouped lists.

members.name: animation
members.description: Reorder animation duration in milliseconds. `0` disables the animation. Reapplied live via `instance.option('animation', v)` (no remount). `options.animation`, and a runtime `option('animation', v)`, win over this prop.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Temporarily disable dragging without unmounting — reapplied live via `instance.option('disabled', v)` (no remount). Also suppresses keyboard reordering: a disabled list is not sortable by any input, so rows lose their `tabindex` and the keydown handler no-ops. Turning it on while a row is lifted ends the lift where the row is (`Lift ended`, and `end` fires); `options.disabled` and `option('disabled', v)` do the same.

members.name: disableKeyboard
members.description: Opt out of keyboard reordering (Space lift / Arrow move / Shift+Arrow hop between lists / Esc cancel / Enter drop) while leaving pointer drag enabled. Rows drop out of the tab order (no `tabindex`) and the keydown handler no-ops. Keyboard access is gated on `!disabled && !disableKeyboard`. Turning it on while a row is lifted ends the lift where the row is.

members.name: keyboardTrigger
members.description: Which element drives keyboard reordering. `'row'` (default): rows are tab stops and the keys on the focused row drive reordering. `'handle'`: rows are NOT tab stops, and only keys pressed inside the element matched by `handle` (inside that row) drive the same Space/Enter lift-drop, Arrow move, Shift+Arrow hop and Escape cancel flow; handled keys call preventDefault so a handle `<button>`'s click does not fire. The consumer owns the handle markup (recommended: a `<button>` with its own aria-label such as "Reorder Hero banner") and the component adds no tabindex or role to slot content. `'handle'` without `handle` turns keyboard reordering off and logs a console warning. `disabled`/`disableKeyboard` still apply. Typed as `SortableKeyboardTrigger` (`'row' | 'handle'`); at runtime any value other than `'handle'` behaves as `'row'`.

members.name: options
members.description: Verbatim SortableJS options pass-through for anything not covered by the named props. The named props win on key conflict but `options` lands AFTER them in the merge so consumers can override defaults; handler keys (`onStart`, `onEnd`, `onUpdate`, `onAdd`, `onRemove`, `onClone`) are stripped — the helper owns those paths. Runtime-updatable: when `options` changes, each key whose value changed is reapplied via `instance.option(key, v)` (no remount), so mouse and keyboard obey the same values; a key you drop goes back to its named prop (or, for `sort` and `draggable`, the component default), and any other dropped key keeps its last value until you set it. `forceFallback` is still read only at construction.

members.name: labelFor
members.description: Optional `(item, idx) => string` returning the screen-reader label for the aria-live announcer during keyboard drag. Defaults to `item.label`; without a `label` field, the row's text (whitespace collapsed, without nested lists or hidden content), else `String(item)` for a primitive, else `item {position}`.

members.name: ghostClass
members.description: Class name applied to the drop-placeholder (ghost) element while dragging. Forwarded live via `instance.option`, so toggling it at runtime takes effect without a remount.

members.name: chosenClass
members.description: Class name applied to the currently-chosen item while dragging. Forwarded live via `instance.option` (no remount needed to change it).

members.name: dragClass
members.description: Class name applied to the dragging element. Only takes effect in fallback mode (`forceFallback: true`). Forwarded live via `instance.option`.

members.name: filter
members.description: CSS selector that prevents drag initiation on matching rows (locked items). SortableJS checks it at `mousedown`/`touchstart` and aborts the drag if it matches. The keyboard honours it too: a row that matches (the row element or its slot root, the element the row template renders) cannot be lifted with Space/Enter; a control nested deeper that matches blocks only presses on it. `options.filter` (which may also be a SortableJS filter function) takes precedence. A `data-*` attribute selector (e.g. `[data-locked]`) is the most robust choice across all targets.

members.name: easing
members.description: CSS easing function for the reorder animation (e.g. `'ease-in'`, `'cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)'`). Runtime-updatable.

members.name: forceFallback
members.description: Force SortableJS's mouse-event drag path over HTML5 DnD — useful for touch devices, consistent cross-browser behavior, and synthetic test drivers (and `dragClass` only applies in this mode). **Construction-time only**: SortableJS reads it once at construction, so re-key the `<SortableList>` to toggle it at runtime.

members.name: swapThreshold
members.description: SortableJS swap threshold (0..1) — a lower value makes rows swap earlier as the dragged item overlaps a neighbor. Reapplied live via `instance.option('swapThreshold', v)` — SortableJS reads it on every dragover, so no remount is needed.

members.name: cloneable
members.description: High-level prop that REPLACES a string `group` with SortableJS's `{ name, pull: 'clone', put: false }` clone-mode object form — the source deposits a COPY onto the destination and keeps its own array unchanged, and takes nothing back: no row can be dropped or keyboard-hopped into it (the palette → canvas pattern). With `group: null` it is a no-op (a clone-mode list with no group name has no peer to clone into). Reapplied live — toggling `cloneable` (or changing `group`) recomputes the clone-mode shape and reapplies it via `instance.option('group', …)`, no remount.

members.name: listClass
members.description: Extra class(es) merged onto the list container (the SortableJS root) alongside the base `rozie-sortable-list` class. Accepts a `String`, `Array`, or `Object` (Vue-style class binding), normalized identically across all six targets — the hook for bridging a CSS framework (`.list-group`) or a flex/grid parent onto the component.

members.name: itemClass
members.description: Extra class(es) merged onto every item row alongside the base `rozie-sortable-item` class. Accepts a `String`, `Array`, or `Object` (Vue-style class binding) applied uniformly, OR an `(item, index) => class` function for per-row classes evaluated at render time. Normalized identically across all six targets.

type.text: string | any[] | Record<string, any> | ((...args: any[]) => any)

members.name: listLabel
members.description: The list's human name, such as `"Top sidebar"`. Sets `aria-label` on the list container (`role="list"`) and names the list in keyboard announcements when a row moves between lists (`Moved Hero banner to Top sidebar, position 1 of 4`, `Dropped Hero banner in Top sidebar at position 3 of 4`, `No list after Top sidebar`). Pass the same words as the zone's visible heading. With no label, announcements fall back to a neutral `list 2 of 3`, counting the mounted lists of the same group in hop (source) order.

members.name: orientation
members.description: Which arrow keys move a lifted row within the list: `'vertical'` (default) uses ↑/↓, `'horizontal'` uses ←/→. A horizontal list's default spoken instructions say "Use the left and right arrow keys to move" (`role="list"` has no `aria-orientation`). Typed as `SortableOrientation` (`'vertical' | 'horizontal'`).

members.name: pageStep
members.description: How many positions Page Up / Page Down move a lifted row. The move stops at the first or last position when fewer rows remain.

members.name: keyboardInstructions
members.description: Replaces the spoken keyboard instructions. The text sits in a hidden element referenced by `aria-describedby` from each tabbable row (row mode) or from the consumer's handle via the `instructionsId` slot prop (handle mode). Default: "Press Space or Enter to pick up, and again to drop. Use the up and down arrow keys to move, Home and End to jump to the start or end, Page Up and Page Down to move several places, and Escape to cancel." (with `orientation: 'horizontal'`, "the left and right arrow keys"; a `sort: false` list says only "Press Space or Enter to pick up, and again to drop. Press Escape to cancel."). When the list has a group (`group` or `options.group`) the default adds "Hold Shift with an arrow key to move to another list."

members.name: announcements
members.description: Rewords or translates what the list says during keyboard reordering. An object of optional functions keyed by message kind (`lifted`, `moved`, `movedToList`, `dropped`, `droppedInList`, `atStart`, `atEnd`, `notSortable`, `noListBefore`, `noListAfter`, `cancelledReturnedToList`, `cancelledReturned`, `cancelledStays`, `cancelledRemoved`, `liftEnded`). Each receives a context (`label`, `item`, `list`, and for kinds with a position `position` (1-based) and `total`; `movedToList` also `fromList`) and returns the text to speak; `null` or `''` says nothing. Kinds without a function keep the default English text (see "Announcements"). Define the object in your script and bind it (Angular templates reject inline arrow functions), e.g. `const announcements = { moved: ({ label, position, total }) => label + ' → ' + position + '/' + total }`. Typed as `Announcements`, exported with `AnnouncementKind` and `AnnouncementContext`.

members.name: itemStyle
members.description: Per-row inline style applied to the `.rozie-sortable-item` wrapper. Accepts a CSS `String`, a flat style object (`Record<string, string | number>`), or an `(item, index) => string | object` function for per-row styling. Because it lands on the wrapper — the direct child of the list container — it can drive CSS-grid placement (`grid-column` / `grid-row` / `align-self`) when `listClass` sets `display: grid`. Normalized per target; `null` / empty drops the attribute.

members.name: getInstance
members.description: Return the underlying SortableJS instance for direct API access (the raw-engine escape hatch — `save`, `closest`, etc. are one hop away). `null` before mount and after destroy.

members.name: toArray
members.description: Return the current order as an array of `data-id` strings (each row carries `data-id="<key>"`). `[]` before mount.

members.name: sort
members.description: Reorder the list by an array of `data-id` strings — `sort(order, useAnimation = true)`.

members.name: option
members.description: Read or set a live SortableJS option — `option(name)` gets, `option(name, value)` sets. The runtime escape hatch for options beyond the curated props.

events.name: reorder
events.description: Fired after the list order changes (same-list reorder commit).

events.name: add
events.description: Fired when an item is added from another list (cross-list destination commit).

events.name: remove
events.description: Fired when an item is moved out to another list (cross-list source commit; not fired in clone mode).

events.name: start
events.description: Fired when a drag starts or a row is lifted by keyboard, from the origin list.

events.name: end
events.description: Fired once when a drag or keyboard lift ends, from the list the row ends up in, after the bound arrays are written.

events.name: items-change
events.description: Fired with the updated `items` (`event.detail`) when it changes.

slots.description: Scoped slot — props: item, index, instructionsId.
